title: [field][Control] onValueChange `value` type

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

The `Field.Control` (`Input`) prop `onValueChange` is incorrect.
The current type of `onValueChange` is as follows:

https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/7ca8cd95a367d60f26265baa4cc539801c398be2/packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx#L162

The `value` argument is set to the following:
```tsx
React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value']
```

The `React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value']` type is a union of four types:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4fd3127-bf27-4219-9224-13803f79ebe2)

This `value` property is what is accepted for an `input` element value **attribute**, but **not** what the HTML element emits as a value in callbacks. For example, the `onChange` callback type is `value: string`.

## Expected behavior

The return type on `onValueChange` should be the `HTMLInputElement['value']`. HTML input elements **never**  invoke callbacks passing  `number | undefined | readonly string[]`, they **only** pass type `string`.

```diff
- onValueChange?: (value: React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value'], event: Event) => void;
+ onValueChange?: (value: HTMLInputElement['value'], event: Event) => void;
```

When performing simple binding with `useState`, type errors are thrown as a simple `string` type is not sufficent to bind as a controlled value. (see example below)

## Reproducible example

[StackBlitz Example](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-yh3fjy2u?file=src%2FInput.tsx)
